research.hours_gaps_limits:
Sessions (index futures, JST), effective since 2024-11-05:
- Day: pre-open 8:00, opening auction 8:45, continuous 8:45-15:40, pre-close 15:40-15:45, closing auction 15:45.
- Night: pre-open 16:45, opening auction 17:00, continuous 17:00-5:55, pre-close 5:55-6:00, closing auction 6:00 the next day.
- No-cancel periods 8:44-8:45 and 5:59-6:00 apply to the Nikkei 225 large/mini/micro group and TOPIX large.
- A trading day runs from the night session through the next day session.
- In 2025 the night session was 40.3% of OSE volume.

Gaps:
- 6:00-8:45 (2h45m) and 15:45-17:00 (1h15m) every day.
- Weekend: Saturday 6:00 to Monday 8:45, about 50h45m.
- Holiday trading has run on most Japanese public holidays since 2022-09-23 (2026 examples: Jan 12, Feb 11, Feb 23, Mar 20, Apr 29, May 4-6, Jul 20).
- Closed at year-end and New Year (2026-01-02 not open).

Structural breaks in intraday history:
- Night session to 3:00 from 2011-07-19.
- Day open 8:45 and night to 5:30 from 2016-07-19.
- Night to 6:00 from 2021-09-21.
- Day close 15:15 to 15:45 and night open 16:30 to 17:00 from 2024-11-05.

Price limits and circuit breakers:
- Daily limits are ±8% of the reference price (Nikkei 225, TOPIX, Growth 250, JPX400). They widen in one direction only, to ±12% and then ±16%, when the circuit breaker triggers.
- Circuit breaker: when the central contract month of the large contract trades or is quoted at the limit, all contract months (including mini and micro) and the related options halt for at least 10 minutes. Trading reopens by auction with the wider limit. It is not applied within 20 minutes of a session's end.
- Dynamic circuit breaker (DCB): an execution beyond ±0.8% of the last price (±3% at the opening auction, ±1.5% at the closing auction) halts trading for at least 30 s.
- Gold mini: ±5%/10%/15%.

Operational gap: kabuステーション logs out at about 6:15 and is usable again from 6:30.
research.kronos_fit:
Pretraining coverage (Kronos paper, Table 13; corpus up to June 2024):
- The only futures were Chinese (75 assets at 1-min, 5-min, 15-min and daily, from 2010). OSE futures were not included.
- Japan was covered by 9 stock indices (5-min to weekly, 2020-01-31 to 2024-06; which 9 is not stated) and 4,467 JPX stocks/ETFs (5-min to weekly), with XJPX used as an in-distribution stock benchmark.
- So Nikkei/TOPIX cash-index and ETF dynamics were seen. Futures-specific structure was not: the 13h night session (17:00-6:00), roll gaps, March/September dividend calendar-spread jumps, and volume/open interest by contract.
- Inputs therefore need a back-adjusted continuous series across rolls, a choice of day-only versus day+night bars, and mini data as a long-history proxy for micro (same price and tick; micro only exists since 2023-05). Amount (turnover) can be built from DataCube VWAP x volume x multiplier.

Breadth: effectively 1-2 instruments (Nikkei 225; TOPIX; the NT spread). Cross-sectional ranking is not possible.

Realistic bar frequency: per-contract commissions do not constrain frequency at this capital, but round-trip cost of about 1.3-3.2 bp does. The IC needed to break even is about cost / (0.8 x sigma over the horizon). Using daily sigma 1.2-1.6%:
- 5-minute bars (sigma about 10-15 bp): IC of about 0.2 or more, which is implausible.
- 1-hour bars (about 30-40 bp): about 0.07.
- Daily bars: about 0.015-0.03.
- The paper's 12-day horizon: about 0.005.

So daily bars, or several hours at a minimum, are realistic. The 512-bar context covers about 2.1 trading days of 5-minute bars (240 bars per trading day including night), 6.4 days of 15-minute bars, 25.6 days of hourly bars, or about 2 years of daily bars (the paper used a 40-day lookback and 12-day horizon). Kronos-small (24.7M parameters) runs on CPU.

Best uses:
1. Volatility or range forecasts to scale a 1-6 micro position (volatility targeting). The paper reports gains in volatility mean absolute error, and volatility is known to be forecastable.
2. Single-instrument direction at a daily or 12-day horizon, as a weak overlay.

Not suitable for cross-sectional ranking.
research.breadth:
Tradeable OSE futures for a small account:
- Nikkei 225 micro: the core instrument. 2025 average daily volume 548k contracts; 2026 to date about 907k.
- Nikkei 225 mini: 2025 ADV 731k, but needs JPY 7-10M or more to size sensibly.
- mini-TOPIX: ADV about 26k; needs JPY 3M or more.
- TSE Growth 250: ADV about 5.9k; the 1-pt tick is about 11-17 bp, which makes it cost-prohibitive.
- JPX-Nikkei 400: ADV about 6.1k.
- OSE DJIA: ADV about 0.9k.
- Gold mini (100 g, JPY 50 tick): ADV about 14k. Not in the kabuステーションAPI product list; IBKR access unverified.
- Pocket Gold 100: launched 2026-04-13, ADV about 0.4k.
- FX futures: launched 2026-04-13, USD/JPY ADV about 0.7k.
- TOPIX large, Nikkei 225 large and JGB contracts are too big.

Effective independent breadth is about 1-2 (Nikkei 225 and TOPIX are both broad Japanese large-cap indices and move closely; the NT ratio is a second, weaker bet). Cross-sectional breadth is zero.
research.edge_plausibility:
Who trades: in 2024, overseas investors made up 70.8% of micro volume, 76.4% of mini, 74.5% of large and 88.9% of mini-TOPIX. Individuals were 29.0%, 20.9%, 8.1% and 7.1% respectively; securities firms' own accounts were 11.4% of large. On OSE financial derivatives, high-frequency traders account for 35-55% of trading value and 93-97% of orders, and supply 60-90% of best-quote liquidity in Nikkei large and mini (FSA, December 2023 data). Sub-minute and short-horizon edges are therefore competed away, and retail traders are mostly liquidity takers.

Literature (all before the sealed window):
- Time-series momentum (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012) is positive across 58 futures, including TOPIX, over 1985-2009. A single instrument is noisy, and replications report it weaker after 2009.
- Intraday momentum (first half-hour predicting last half-hour) was shown for the US SPY ETF (Gao et al. 2018). Across 12 international index futures, Liu and Tse (2017) found no first-half-hour effect, but overnight returns did predict the last half-hour.
- Volatility is forecastable (HAR model, Corsi 2009). Volatility-managed exposure helped in-sample (Moreira-Muir 2017), but out-of-sample gains are disputed (Cederburg et al. 2020).

Arithmetic, with breadth 1 and IC about 0.02:
- 12-day bets (about 21 per year): IR is about 0.02 x √21 ≈ 0.09.
- Daily bets: gross IR is about 0.3, but around 1 bp/day of turnover cost roughly halves it.
- Either way, an edge would take decades to detect statistically. A weeks-long forward test can validate execution and costs only, not edge.

Plausibility: an edge here needs either IC of about 0.05 or more at a daily horizon, or a risk/sizing benefit (volatility targeting) rather than direction. Transaction costs (about 1.3-3.2 bp per micro round trip) are not the binding constraint at daily horizons.
risks: Leverage and gap risk. Night-session news, the weekend gap (about 50h45m), holidays, ±8-16% limit moves and circuit-breaker halts. Stop orders can fill far beyond the stop. One 8% move costs about 6-9% of JPY 500k per micro.

Margin calls. JSCC VaR margins reset daily and use EWMA volatility scaling, so they can jump in volatile periods. At eSmart a shortfall must be covered by noon the next business day, otherwise all positions are force-closed.

Operations. kabuステーション needs Windows 11, an always-on PC and a manual login every day (logout about 6:15, no official auto-login or reconnect). IBKR needs a weekly 2FA login. The laptop has to be always on, or a paid VPS or Windows VM is needed (cost outside the stated budget categories).

API terms. eSmart bans third-party programs, continuous storage of API or chart data, editing it, and feeding it into external AI services. Research history must come from DataCube or J-Quants. Logging quotes in a forward test is limited to temporary storage, and whether stored Kronos predictions count as processed data is unclear.
No realistic paper environment at eSmart. IBKR paper fills are simulated and optimistic about queue position and fills. The forward test should be live with 1 micro or a shadow mode.

Data budget. J-Quants futures data needs JPY 16,500/month. DataCube history is a one-off JPY 15-50k. IBKR cannot supply contracts that expired before about Nov 2024. All of these exceed or sit outside the JPY 3,000/month without approval.

Distribution shift. Kronos never saw OSE futures (night session, rolls, dividend calendar spreads). Session-time changes in 2016, 2021 and 2024, and holiday trading from 2022, break intraday history. Micro exists only since 2023-05, so mini data must stand in for it.
Statistical power. With breadth of about 1, an IC near 0.02 cannot be told apart from zero in a forward test, and there is a high risk of overfitting a single price path.

Tax. Futures gains are taxed separately at 20.315%, and losses offset only other 先物取引に係る雑所得等 (3-year carry-forward). They cannot offset crypto, which is currently 雑所得 taxed at progressive rates. Separate 20% taxation for designated crypto (特定暗号資産) is expected from 2028; spot-crypto losses would offset only within spot crypto, and how it interacts with futures is unclear.

Eligibility. F/O account screening (eSmart) requires experience in stocks, F&O, CFD or FX and sufficient income or assets; crypto experience is not listed. IBKR's futures permission criteria are unknown.

Platform change. J-GATE 4.0 (Nasdaq) is planned for late 2028, which will likely force broker API changes. The JSCC VaR software was upgraded to v4.0 on 2026-04-13, and the market-maker program was revised effective 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-19. Spread and depth conditions can change.
Liquidity pockets. Micro depth by session and contract month is unpublished, and market makers may quote up to 4-6 ticks wide. Night-session and SQ/roll-day slippage is unmeasured.
Continuous-series construction. Naive splicing across rolls, especially the March and September dividend-driven calendar spreads, creates false jumps and false signals.
open_questions: What are micro's actual quoted spread and top-of-book depth by session (day, night, holiday) and by contract month? Which micro month (nearest monthly or nearest quarterly) is the central, most liquid one, and when is the best roll date?

IBKR Japan: what are the futures permission criteria and minimum deposit for individuals? What margin multiplier applies to OSE futures relative to JSCC? Does the JPY 10/contract overnight fee (Tiered) apply to micro? Is the OSE data fee waivable through commissions? How realistic are OSE micro fills in the paper account?

eSmart: what exact limit separates allowed temporary storage from prohibited continuous storage of API data? This was asked publicly on 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-30 and was unanswered when fetched. May derived features and model predictions be stored?
Can kabuステーションAPI place orders in holiday sessions? Are stop orders (逆指値) held on the broker's server or at the exchange, and how do they behave at session opens and gaps?

Budget: does the JPY 3,000/month limit cover hosting (an always-on Linux or Windows host)? Is a one-off DataCube purchase (about JPY 15-50k) or one month of J-Quants Premium (JPY 16,500) approved? May J-Quants data be kept after cancelling?
Which 9 Japanese indices were in Kronos pretraining (Nikkei 225, TOPIX?) and at which frequencies? The paper's Table 13 gives counts only.
Is interest paid on cash held as futures margin at eSmart or IBKR?
Does the user meet F/O account screening, i.e. prior experience in stocks, FX or CFD?
How will the 2028 crypto tax regime categorise crypto derivatives relative to 先物取引に係る雑所得等, and could the two offset each other?
Gold mini: which API broker supports it (eSmart: no; IBKR: unverified; 楽天 RSS: unknown)?

claims.claim: Nikkei 225 micro futures: launched 2023-05-29; contract unit Nikkei 225 x JPY 10; tick JPY 5 (JPY 50 per contract); contract months are the nearest 2 quarterly and nearest 2 monthly; cash-settled at SQ (opening prices of constituents on the 2nd Friday; last trading day is the business day before); holiday trading available; calendar-spread trading available.

Nikkei 225 mini: Nikkei 225 x JPY 100, tick JPY 5 (JPY 500 per contract); quarterly months (June/December nearest 10, March/September nearest 3) plus nearest 3 monthly months. Nikkei 225 large: x JPY 1,000, tick JPY 10.

mini-TOPIX: TOPIX x JPY 1,000, tick 0.25 pt (JPY 250), 3 quarterly months. TSE Growth 250 futures: index x JPY 1,000, tick 1 pt (JPY 1,000), 5 quarterly months. JPX-Nikkei 400: x JPY 100, tick 5 pt (JPY 500).

Index-futures sessions (JST): day pre-open 8:00, opening auction 8:45, continuous 8:45-15:40, closing auction 15:45; night pre-open 16:45, opening auction 17:00, continuous 17:00-5:55, closing auction 6:00. These times are in effect since 2024-11-05 under the OSE rule revision.

Earlier session structure: night session to 3:00 from 2011-07-19; day open 8:45 and night to 5:30 from 2016-07-19; night to 6:00 from 2021-09-21; holiday trading from 2022-09-23. Before 2024-11-05 the day close was 15:15 and the night open 16:30 (these earlier times are inferred, not stated in the revision document).

Price limits for Nikkei 225 (large, mini, micro), TOPIX, mini-TOPIX, Growth 250 and JPX400 futures are ±8% normally, then ±12% and ±16%, widened in one direction only. The circuit breaker is triggered by the large contract's central month at the limit; it halts all months, including mini and micro, for at least 10 minutes, and is not applied within 20 minutes of a session's end. The dynamic circuit breaker is ±0.8% of the last price (±3% at the opening auction, ±1.5% at the closing auction) with halts of at least 30 s.

JSCC has used VaR margining since 2023-11-06: historical-simulation VaR at 97.5% expected shortfall (about 99% coverage), a 2-day margin period of risk, a 1,250-day lookback with EWMA volatility scaling, and stress-day scenarios since 2008. The VaR software was upgraded to v4.0 on 2026-04-13.

Exchange margin per contract (Dec-2026 contract, short / long) on 2026-11-06: micro JPY 41,312 / 45,157; mini JPY 413,116 / 451,566; mini-TOPIX JPY 184,930 / 232,731; Growth 250 JPY 54,154 / 64,419; JPX400 JPY 163,793 / 206,815; large JPY 4,131,151 / 4,515,655. These change daily.

三菱UFJ eスマート証券 futures commissions per contract per side, tax included: micro JPY 11; mini JPY 38.5 (JPY 27.5 if SOR/J-NET matched); large JPY 275; mini-TOPIX, JPX400, Growth 250, REIT and Core30 JPY 41.8; TOPIX JPY 330. The same fees apply on every channel. Required margin = VaR margin x 100% minus net option value.

kabuステーションAPI is a REST and PUSH API served locally by the kabuステーション app (production port 18080, test port 18081). It accepts requests only from the same IP/PC, and kabuステーション requires Windows 11 (8 GB memory or more). Use requires the Professional or Premium plan (Professional: margin or F/O account plus at least 1 execution in roughly the past 3 months).
The kabuステーションAPI test environment always returns fixed values only, so there is no paper trading or simulated fills.

kabuステーション logs out automatically every day (usable 6:30 to 6:15 the next morning). The user must log in manually after logout or a reboot; the broker provides no auto-start or reconnect function. Orders already accepted stay valid if the app stops.

kabuステーションAPI limits: orders 10 requests/s; info and wallet about 10 requests/s; time and sales 2 requests/s; at most 50 registered symbols; PUSH throttled to 400 ms; 10-level board. Futures order types: limit (FAS/FAK/FOK), market (FAK/FOK), stop-limit, stop-market, market-on-close and limit-on-close, routable to day, night or all-day sessions. Supported codes include NK225micro, NK225mini, TOPIXmini and GROWTH.

checks.correction: All-day (日通し) routing is allowed only for limit FAS and stop-limit FAS. Limit FAK/FOK, market FAK/FOK, stop-market (FAK), 引成 (FAK) and 引指 (FAS) can be sent only to the day or the night session. On the last trading day, DerivMonth=0 returns the expiring contract, whose trading ends with that day session.

claims.claim: kabuステーション terms (Art. 4) prohibit accumulating, editing or processing, and secondary use of the information. eSmart states that continuous storage of API or chart data is not permitted (temporary storage on the API PC is OK, as are logs and the user's own trade records), and that API data must not be input into external AI services. Third-party programs are prohibited; AI-assisted code written by the user is allowed.

eSmart futures/options account screening: age 18+, sufficient income or financial assets, investment objective 収益性重視 or 安定性・収益性重視, and experience with stocks, futures, options, CFD or FX plus knowledge. Position limit is 200 contracts per side in large-equivalent (micro counts 0.01). A margin shortfall must be met by noon the next business day, otherwise positions are force-closed.

IBKR証券 OSE futures commissions per side, including tax: micro Fixed JPY 14 or Tiered JPY 15 (up to 10,000 contracts/month) plus exchange and clearing fees; mini Fixed JPY 40 or Tiered JPY 28; mini-TOPIX, Growth 250 and JPX400 Fixed JPY 50 or Tiered JPY 38; N225 large Fixed JPY 400 or Tiered JPY 280. In IBKR's large-contract example, an overnight position adds JPY 10 per contract.

checks.correction: Exchange and clearing fees are added only on Tiered pricing; Fixed is all-in. IBKR's examples: Fixed N225 round trip = JPY 800 (2 x 400). Tiered N225 = 280 + 110 exchange + 20 clearing = JPY 410 per side, plus JPY 10 per contract if held overnight. A Fixed micro round trip is therefore JPY 28 all-in, versus JPY 22 at eSmart.

claims.claim: IBKR market data for the Osaka Exchange: L1 JPY 200/month and L2 JPY 400/month for non-professionals. Delayed data (20 minutes) is free.

IBKR offers the TWS API (through TWS or IB Gateway) and a Web API (REST plus WebSocket) to individual clients. IB Gateway installers exist for Linux x86_64 and ARM64. The TWS API accepts up to 50 messages/s.
An IBKR paper trading account is available after the live account is approved (no immediate funding needed), with USD 1M of simulated funds.
TWS and IB Gateway must auto-restart daily, and a manual login (with 2FA) is required once a week.
IBKR historical data excludes expired futures more than 2 years after expiry, and bars of 30 s or less older than 6 months.

Tachibana e支店 API v4r10 (current from 2026-09-27) has order functions only for domestic stocks (cash and margin); for futures and options it offers only master-data queries. OSE futures cannot be traded through it.

楽天 Market Speed II RSS includes futures/options order functions (RssFOPOpenOrder and related) but works only in Microsoft Excel on Windows (not on Mac). 楽天 fees: micro JPY 11, mini JPY 38.5, Growth 250 JPY 41.8.

checks.correction: Fees are confirmed. The RSS platform restriction is unverified in this pass.

claims.claim: J-Quants: futures OHLC (先物四本値) is available only on the Premium plan at JPY 16,500/month; Light is JPY 1,650 and Standard JPY 3,300. Futures data is per contract with whole-day, day-session and night-session OHLC, volume, open interest and settlement, from 2008-05-07 (micro from 2023-05-29; Growth from 2016-07-19). Daily only.

checks.correction: The settlement-price field exists only from 2016-07-19. Before 2011-02-10 the day-session fields hold the afternoon session only (the morning session is not recorded). Holiday-session trades are merged into the adjacent trading day. Days with emergency margin produce duplicate rows (EmMrgnTrgDiv).

claims.claim: J-Quants DataCube sells per-product monthly files at personal prices: futures daily JPY 110, 1-minute JPY 220, tick JPY 330. Nikkei 225 large and mini 1-minute data runs from 2012-01 (yearly files 2007-2011 at JPY 2,640), micro from 2023-05. Files include all contract months listed that month, with day and night session IDs; no later corrections; trades only.
The DataCube 自己使用（個人） licence covers only the buyer's own private asset management, with no business use and no provision to third parties beyond small quotations.

Kronos pretraining corpus (data to June 2024; Table 13): futures only from China (75 assets; 1-min, 5-min, 15-min and daily; from 2010); Japan covered by 9 stock indices (5-min to weekly, from 2020-01-31) and 4,467 JPX stocks/ETFs (5-min to weekly). OSE futures are not listed.

2025 average daily volume: micro 548,368; mini 731,401; large 61,017; TOPIX 85,679; mini-TOPIX 25,762; Growth 250 5,928; JPX400 6,122; gold mini 14,193. Micro 2026 year to date (180 trading days): 906,651.

Share of trading volume by investor type, 2024: micro 70.8% overseas / 29.0% individuals; mini 76.4% / 20.9%; large 74.5% / 8.1% (securities firms 11.4%); mini-TOPIX 88.9% / 7.1%; Growth 250 56.4% / 25.8%.

On OSE financial derivatives, high-frequency traders account for 35-55% of trading value and 93-97% of orders. Their liquidity provision ratio at the best quotes is 0.6-0.9 (large) and 0.6-0.8 (mini), from December 2023 order data.
The night session made up 40.3% of OSE trading volume in 2025.

Market-maker obligations: micro maximum spread 4 ticks (JPY 20) in the nearest quarterly month (day and night) and 6 ticks in the nearest monthly month (day), minimum 50 contracts; mini-TOPIX 4 ticks (1.00 pt); Growth 250 8 ticks (8 pts), day session; mini monthly 6 ticks. Revised 2026-10-01, effective 2026-11-02.

JPX research on Nikkei 225 mini in normal 2025 periods: average relative spread about 0.000144 (1.44 bp, about one tick) and about 65 contracts at the best quotes. No comparable statistic was found for micro.

checks.correction: The baseline period is 2025-01-06 to 2025-04-30, excluding an event window of 2025-04-02 to 2025-04-16. Depth is the mean of best-bid and best-ask sizes, about 65 per side. 'About one tick' is not stated and would need a price level. The report's data period and its subject (market behaviour in April 2025) lie inside the sealed window, so treat it as a contaminated source. No micro statistic exists in it.

claims.claim: Futures gains are taxed separately as 先物取引に係る雑所得等 at 15% income tax plus 5% local tax (plus reconstruction tax; from 2027 reconstruction tax 1.1% plus defense tax 1%). Losses offset only within that category and can be carried forward 3 years.

Crypto gains are currently 雑所得 taxed at progressive rates. Separate 20% taxation for designated crypto (特定暗号資産) spot, funds and derivatives is planned, expected in 2028; spot-crypto losses would offset only within spot crypto.

checks.correction: The start date is 1 January of the year after the amended FIEA takes effect, not a fixed 2028. Crypto derivatives would then share a tax bucket with OSE futures, so their gains and losses would offset each other.
checks.source: 令和8年度税制改正の大綱 (財務省, 閣議決定 2025-12-26); local copy <scratch>/phase0/mof_taikou_r8.txt

claims.claim: OSE plans to replace J-GATE 3.0 with J-GATE 4.0 (vendor Nasdaq) around late 2028.
TOPIX futures excess returns had long-run annualised volatility of 18.66% (sample from July 1976, paper sample to 2009). This is used here as the pre-window risk assumption (daily sigma about 1.2%).

Gold mini futures: 100 g, cash-settled against the Gold Standard futures price, tick JPY 0.5/g (JPY 50), nearest 6 even months, ±5%/10%/15% limits, same day/night hours as index futures. The kabuステーションAPI FutureCode list contains no commodities.

New OSE products launched 2026-04-13: USD/JPY, CNH/JPY and EUR/JPY futures (USD 10,000 unit, JPY 0.01 tick) and Pocket Gold/Platinum 100. Year-to-date average daily volume: USD/JPY about 702, Pocket Gold 100 about 393 contracts.

checks.correction: The units and ticks differ by pair: USD/JPY is USD 10,000 with a JPY 0.01 tick; EUR/JPY is EUR 10,000 with JPY 0.01; CNH/JPY is CNH 100,000 with JPY 0.001.

claims.claim: Brokers listed by JPX as offering Nikkei 225 micro to individuals: IBKR証券, SBI証券, 三菱UFJ eスマート証券, 光世証券, フィリップ・キャピタル証券, 松井証券, マネックス証券, 楽天証券.

Volatility literature: volatility is forecastable with a HAR model (Corsi 2009). Volatility-managed portfolios (Moreira-Muir 2017) improve in-sample performance, but out-of-sample gains are disputed (Cederburg et al. 2020). Intraday momentum (Gao et al. 2018) was shown for the US SPY ETF.

new_findings.finding: The kabuステーション terms block the natural live-data pipeline. API policy Art. 3-2 (revised 2025-02-05) bans 転載 to any terminal other than the one displaying the data. User policy Art. 4 (revised 2025-08) bans 蓄積, 編集加工 and 二次利用. eSmart's official reply on 2026-10-16 allows only 'temporary' storage on the API PC and gives no threshold (follow-ups unanswered as of 2026-10-30). API v1.5 also has no historical-bar endpoint: its endpoints are token, sendorder, cancelorder, wallet, board, symbol, orders, positions, register, symbolname, ranking, exchange, regulations, timeandsales and similar.
new_findings.impact: On the eSmart route, Kronos has to run on the same Windows 11 PC, not the Linux laptop. Its 40-512-bar context cannot be built by accumulating API bars. Licensed history must come from DataCube, whose monthly files arrive by the 5th business day of the next month (up to about 5 weeks stale), or from J-Quants Premium (daily, JPY 16,500/month, over budget). The cheapest route therefore has an unresolved live-data gap. IBKR, which serves historical bars through its API, may be the only within-budget path for both data and execution, at JPY 28 versus JPY 22 per micro round trip plus JPY 200/month. Whether IBKR needs the L1 subscription for API history was not verified.

new_findings.finding: eSmart margin rules (2026-08): closing part of a position does not cure a margin shortfall. If the shortfall is not met by 12:00 the next business day, all positions are force-closed after 12:00. Unrealised losses must be covered in cash, not substitute securities. Required margin is VaR x a broker-set multiplier (currently 100%), which eSmart can change.
new_findings.impact: VaR margin is about JPY 41-45k per micro (2026-11-06), so margin itself does not bind at JPY 500k. But any shortfall means full liquidation, not a partial cut, so sizing should keep a cash buffer well above VaR margin. Margin can rise at the broker's discretion.

new_findings.finding: The micro's daily settlement price and SQ are defined as identical to the same-month Nikkei 225 mini, and both use a JPY 5 tick.
new_findings.impact: Mini history is an exact price proxy for the micro before its 2023-05 listing. Sources: DataCube mini 1-minute data from 2012-01 plus yearly files from 2007, mini tick data from 2006-07, J-Quants daily from 2008-05-07. This removes the short-history limit for price-based modelling; volume series differ.

new_findings.finding: Official futures history is not homogeneous across time. Session hours changed on 2011-07-19, 2016-07-19, 2021-09-21 and 2024-11-05. Holiday sessions started 2022-09-23; they carry DataCube Session_ID 003 and are merged into the adjacent trading day. DataCube 1-minute OHLC and volume include strategy trades through 2021-09-17 and exclude them from 2021-09-21. The DataCube VWAP definition changed 2014-03-24. In J-Quants, the day fields before 2011-02-10 hold the afternoon session only, and settlement prices exist only from 2016-07-19.
new_findings.impact: Daily bars built over 2008-2026 have changing composition. The pre-registration must fix the bar construction (for example, whole trading days built from 1-minute data with an explicit session mapping) and may need to start training after 2016-07-19 or 2021-09-21, or test that the results are robust to the start date.

new_findings.finding: OSE primary market makers only need to meet the maximum spread at a performance rate of 50-60%. The mini has a quoting obligation only in its nearest monthly contract, not the quarterly one.
new_findings.impact: The 4- and 6-tick market-maker caps are not a continuous spread guarantee. The cost model should use measured pre-window spreads, not the market-maker maximum.

new_findings.finding: rerk2511.pdf (JPX 先物・オプションレポート 2025年11月号), the source for OSEFUT-33, is about market behaviour in April 2025, and its statistics come from January to April 2025. All of this is inside the sealed 2024-07-01 to 2026-10-31 window.
new_findings.impact: Pre-registration hygiene: do not reuse this report beyond the bare spread and depth figures. A pre-July-2024 spread statistic would be cleaner for the cost model.

new_findings.finding: The FY2026 tax reform outline (Cabinet decision 2025-12-26) moves derivatives on specified crypto (特定暗号資産デリバティブ取引) into the 先物取引に係る雑所得等 regime. This applies from 1 January of the year after the amended FIEA takes effect. Until then, crypto is 総合課税 雑所得 and cannot offset futures losses (NTA 1521).
new_findings.impact: From that date, crypto-derivative P&L shares one tax bucket with OSE futures, so gains and losses offset and carry forward 3 years. Before that date there is no cross-offset. This changes after-tax evaluation only and does not block feasibility.
new_findings.source: 令和8年度税制改正の大綱 (財務省, 2025-12-26; local copy <scratch>/phase0/mof_taikou_r8.txt) ; https://www.nta.go.jp/taxes/shiraberu/taxanswer/shotoku/1521.htm

new_findings.finding:
Operational traps on the eSmart and OSE path:
- On the last trading day, the API's DerivMonth=0 returns the expiring contract, which stops trading after that day session.
- All-day routing is limited to limit FAS and stop-limit orders.
- No orders can be placed for about 5 minutes from 0:00.
- kabuステーション logs out daily at 6:15, so a manual login is needed before the 8:45 open.
- No holiday session is held on a contract's first trading day, last trading day or SQ day.
- On holiday sessions, DCB halts are longer and the price-limit reference price is not updated.
new_findings.impact: The forward test must handle roll and expiry logic, session-specific order routing and a daily manual login. These raise operating burden but do not block the route.

new_findings.finding: J-Quants Light (JPY 1,650/month, within budget) includes daily TOPIX OHLC with 5 years of history. Standard (JPY 3,300, just over budget) adds other index OHLC. Neither plan includes futures or night sessions.
new_findings.impact: A cheap source of underlying-index daily bars for features or cross-checks, but not a substitute for futures data. Impact is low.

title: Retail OTC FX for Japan residents

research.market: Retail OTC FX (店頭外国為替証拠金取引, spot FX on margin) for a Japan-resident individual
research.summary:
Verdict: feasible. On operations and cost, FX is the easiest candidate market. As a Kronos test, especially a cross-sectional one, it is statistically the weakest.

(1) API. The cleanest route is GMO Coin's 外国為替FX API. It is REST plus WebSocket, runs natively on Linux, and needs no local app. It needs a GMO Coin membership plus a separate FX account application. API new orders start at 100 units for majors and 10,000 units for TRY, ZAR, MXN, HUF, SEK and NOK/SEK. There is no commission. Each API order that fills pays an API fee of 0.002% of notional, which is 0.4 bps per round trip (FX-4). The first 30 days after the first FX API key are free. There are 21 pairs now; 14 existed before May 2026. There is no sandbox.

The second route is Saxo Bank Securities (サクソバンク証券) OpenAPI. It is REST/WebSocket with a SIM environment, has no minimum deposit, and is free for private use. Saxo states it does not support OpenAPI (technical help in English only).

OANDA's v20 REST API needs Gold status, which means at least US$500k of trading in the prior month, plus ¥250k and the Pro course. That is impractical at ¥0.5–3M. OANDA, FXTF, JFX, 外為ファイネスト, 楽天 and AvaTrade otherwise offer only MT4/MT5, which is Windows-only: the MetaTrader5 Python package ships only win_amd64 wheels. IG証券 offers no API. IBSJ does not offer FX trading. No retail API was found for くりっく365.

(2) Capital does not bind. Margin is 4% (the 25x cap). A 10-currency long-short book at about ¥100k notional per position needs about ¥40–50k of margin. This is feasible at ¥500k, ¥1M and ¥3M.

(3) Costs. In liquid hours, majors cost about 0.6–1.3 bps per round trip (spread plus API fee). GMO's spreads are variable and unpublished, so the only figures found are third-party and low confidence. NZD/JPY and GBP/USD are about 2 bps, MXN/JPY about 3, ZAR/JPY about 12 and TRY/JPY about 120. All bps figures use assumed price levels. Spreads blow out around the NY close and early Tokyo hours: Saxo's USD/JPY goes from 0.2 sen to 60 sen between 04:00 and 07:59 JST. The bigger hidden cost is the swap asymmetry, estimated at 0.15–0.2 bps per day per position. Shorting is free and symmetric.

(4) Data is free and deep:
- Dukascopy bid/ask ticks from 2003.
- HistData M1 bars from 2000.
- GMO Coin's own BID/ASK bars from 2023-01-02. Daily bars start at 06:00 JST year-round, five bars per week, with no volume field.

FX has no delistings and no corporate actions.

(5) Kronos fit. FX was in pretraining: over 1,000 pairs, OHLC only, which matches GMO's volume-less bars. The daily setting (lookback 40, horizon 12) is realistic. But GMO Coin offers only 10 currencies against JPY during the study windows. With 10 names, a 12-day cross-sectional RankIC needs IC ≈ 0.16 to reach Newey-West t ≥ 3 on the dev window, or about 0.05 at a 1-day horizon. Both are far above the roughly 0.02 seen elsewhere (my own power estimate). The best-fitting use is volatility forecasts for position sizing, tested against HAR-RV. The literature prior for a directional edge is low.

(6) Key structural risk. Under GMO Coin's contract, it can freeze and dispose of cash and crypto held in the same GMO Coin account to cover unpaid FX debt. That links FX gap risk to everything else held there.

Pick FX if the study's main question is volatility for sizing. As a return-ranking market it has low expected value.

capital.sensible_book:
Two definitions, both feasible:
- (a) Cross-sectional: every tradeable currency against JPY in a long-short book, roughly equal in risk, with about ¥50–150k notional per position and gross exposure ≤3x capital. That is 10 currencies for the study windows (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CAD, CHF, TRY, ZAR, MXN) and 13 since 2026-05-18 (adding HUF, SEK, and NOK via NOK/SEK).
- (b) Single instrument (e.g. USD/JPY or EUR/USD), volatility-targeted, with ≤1–2% of capital at risk per trade. Example: 1% of ¥500k with a stop at 2× the 12-day sigma (0.6%/day assumed) gives about ¥120k notional, or about 800 USD units. The 1–100 unit granularity makes this easy.
capital.capital_needed_jpy: Technically about ¥300k is enough: a 10-position book at about ¥80–100k each is ¥0.8–1.0M gross, needing about ¥32–40k maintenance margin at 4% or ¥40–50k order margin at 5%. ¥500k is comfortable, with a maintenance ratio of about 1,000–1,250% at 2x gross. Capital is not a binding constraint at any of the three levels.
capital.at_500k: Feasible. 2–3x gross for a 10-currency book. Exotic 10,000-unit lots (ZAR, MXN, TRY) fit. Single-instrument risk of 1–2% per trade is easy to size.
capital.at_1m: Feasible. Roughly 1–1.5x gross for the same book. Room to keep the FX account well above loss-cut, or to fund a second broker (Saxo) for wider breadth.
capital.at_3m: Feasible. Gross can stay below 1x. The 25x cap is irrelevant. OANDA's v20 API is still impractical: Gold needs US$500k a month in volume, about 25x this capital in monthly turnover.

costs.breakdown:
- Commission: 0 (GMO, Saxo, OANDA Tokyo).
- GMO API fee: 0.002% of executed notional per API order that fills, i.e. 0.2 bps per side. Closing orders sent via API are charged too. Free for 30 days after the first FX API key.
- Spread: GMO variable and unpublished; Saxo fixed in core hours for 5 pairs.
- Slippage: market orders fill at the price when processed. GMO's speedOrder accepts a slippage bound; orders outside the bound expire.
- No exchange or clearing fees, no stamp duty.
- Loss-cut fee: ¥0.05 per unit, only on forced liquidation (about 3 bps on USD/JPY at 150).
- Tax (separate from costs): gains taxed at 20.315% under separate self-assessment.
costs.holding_costs:
Swap points are the only carry cost; there is no margin interest, no borrow fee and no futures roll (spot rolls automatically each day).
- Mechanics at GMO: swaps quoted per 10,000 units (100,000 for TRY, ZAR, MXN, HUF, SEK, NOK/SEK). Credited or debited after 06:00 JST and paid on settlement. Weekends and holidays are booked as 3–4 days at once. Can change sign. A daily history is published.
- Economics: about the interest differential, minus a dealer markup that makes buy and sell swaps asymmetric.
- Markup estimate: a third-party GMO Coin snapshot from 2023-11-25 (low confidence) implies about 0.15–0.2 bps per day per position for majors. That is ≈2.5–3.4 bps per 12-trading-day hold (≈17 calendar days), larger than the spread plus fee.
- Shorting a high-yielder: pays the full differential, which is large for TRY, ZAR and MXN.
- Backtests need actual swap histories. The GMO calendar has past swaps. An alternative is policy or OIS rate differentials minus an assumed markup.

research.shorting:
Yes, and symmetric: any pair can be sold at the same 4% margin. There is no borrow, no locate, no uptick rule, and no short-sale ban in OTC FX.

The cost is the swap: being short the higher-yielding currency pays the interest differential, plus the buy/sell swap markup. For EM currencies (TRY, ZAR, MXN) that carry is large.

GMO Coin allows hedged positions (両建て; isHedgeable flag), though they are uneconomic.

Restrictions:
- Dealers can suspend new orders in a pair; GMO's API has ERR-143 '規制中のため取引できない'.
- GMO's API minimum for exotics is 10,000 units.
- Loss-cut at a 100% maintenance ratio applies to longs and shorts alike.

research.hours_gaps_limits:
Trading hours:
- GMO Coin FX trades Monday 07:00 to Saturday 05:59 JST, stated as fixed with no daylight-saving variation. Christmas and New Year hours can differ. Orders are accepted 24/7 except during maintenance, which runs regularly on Saturdays. The daily candle and the swap both roll at 06:00 JST.
- Saxo accepts orders from Monday 03:00 or 04:00 JST to Saturday 05:59 or 06:59 JST, depending on Australian and US daylight saving. Maintenance is at weekends.

Overnight and weekend gaps:
- FX trades through the night, so the overnight gap is a liquidity hole rather than a closure.
- Around the NY close and rollover (about 05:00–08:00/09:00 JST), dealers' fixed-spread guarantees lapse and spreads widen. Saxo's USD/JPY goes from 0.2 sen to 60 sen between 04:00 and 07:59 JST. GMOクリック quotes 3.8 sen outside 09:00–27:00 JST.
- At GMO, the weekend closure lasts about 49 hours (Sat 05:59 to Mon 07:00 JST), so Monday-open gaps and holiday thin-liquidity events matter. Example: the 2019-01-03 yen flash event at the Asian open, which the RBA linked partly to Japanese retail automatic orders and thin liquidity.

Implication for the study: a daily signal at the 06:00 JST bar close should not be filled 'at the next open'. Fill it in the 08:00/09:00+ JST window, and model that lag.

Price limits and circuit breakers:
- OTC FX has no daily price limits and no circuit breakers.
- Dealers may stop streaming prices in extreme moves. Resting limit and stop orders then fill at the resumption price (per GMO's 説明書).
- GMO rejects orders priced outside mid ±10%.
- Loss-cut triggers when the maintenance ratio falls below 100% at GMO, but execution takes time, so losses beyond margin and a negative balance are possible.
research.kronos_fit:
In pretraining: yes.
- The corpus included 'a comprehensive dataset of over 1,000 foreign exchange pairs', OHLC only, with volume and amount deliberately excluded. FX was upweighted during pretraining, which ends June 2024.
- KronosPredictor fills missing volume and amount with zeros, which matches GMO's volume-less bars.
- Kronos also feeds timestamp features (minute, hour, weekday, day, month). The daily-bar convention therefore changes the inputs: GMO opens bars at 06:00 JST year-round, Dukascopy defaults to UTC midnight, HistData uses EST without DST. Pre-register one convention.
- The paper's FX vendor and session conventions are undisclosed.
- The paper's own FX tests use a test period starting July 2024. That overlaps the sealed window, so they were not read or reported.

Breadth: 10 currencies vs JPY at GMO Coin for the study windows (13 since 2026-05-18); effectively fewer (see breadth).

Bar frequency:
- Daily (lookback 40, horizon 12) is realistic and matches the paper. Major-pair costs of about 1 bp per round trip, plus about 0.2 bps a day in swap markup, allow daily rebalancing.
- 1h or 4h bars are cost-feasible on majors but add time-of-day spread regimes and are not needed.
- Compute is small: about 10–14 series × about 460 dev days per variant.

Which use fits:
1. Volatility forecasts for sizing: best fit. FX volatility clusters strongly, and free tick/M1 data makes HAR-RV, EWMA and GARCH baselines exact.
2. Cross-sectional ranking: cheap to run but badly underpowered. My own estimate assumes the RankIC standard error is about 1/√(N−1) ≈ 0.33 with N = 10 and about 460 dev days. On that basis, Newey-West t ≥ 3 needs a mean IC of about 0.05 at a 1-day horizon, or about 0.16 at a 12-day horizon (about 38 effective periods).
3. Single-instrument direction: weakest. For a 1-day time-series correlation, the standard error over 460 days is about 0.047.
research.breadth:
GMO Coin lists 21 pairs now; 14 during the pre-registered windows. The currencies are JPY, USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CAD, CHF, TRY, ZAR and MXN, so 10 independent exchange rates. From 2026-05-18 HUF, SEK and NOK (via NOK/SEK) bring it to 13.

Cost limits the useful set further:
- 7 G10 currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CAD, CHF) trade at about 1–2 bps per round trip.
- 3 EM currencies are expensive: MXN about 3 bps, ZAR about 12, TRY about 120.

Effective breadth is lower still:
- Every JPY cross shares the JPY leg.
- Two global factors, dollar and carry, account for 18% to 80% of monthly bilateral exchange-rate movements (Verdelhan 2018).

Other brokers:
- Saxo lists 155 pairs, perhaps 30–40 currencies, but EM spreads are wide and the API is unsupported.
- OANDA NY lists 68 pairs (API gated); OANDA Tokyo 37–40.

Illustrative fundamental-law arithmetic, assuming independent bets and before costs: IC = 0.02 with N = 10 gives an annual information ratio of about 0.3 at a 12-day horizon, and about 1.0 only with fully independent daily bets. US stocks with N = 500 would give about 2.0.
research.edge_plausibility:
Low for direction, moderate for volatility sizing.

Market structure:
- Global FX turnover was $9.6 trillion per day in April 2025 (BIS preliminary; $9.5 trillion final). The US dollar is on one side of 89% of trades. The market is dominated by dealers and institutions and is highly electronic.
- Algorithmic and high-frequency trading are major interdealer participants (Chaboud et al. 2014, JF; BIS QR Dec 2010 names HFT and online retail as growth drivers).
- Japanese retail is large in yen. Retail OTC FX customer volume was ¥1,472 trillion in April 2025. Dealers' external cover flow was about 112% of Tokyo spot turnover, and dealers covered only about 30.5% of customer volume externally, internalising about 70% (FFAJ 2025).
- Retail traders lose on average (Heimer & Simsek 2019, JFE). Their clustered stop orders can amplify flash events (RBA 2019).

Predictability literature (pre-2024):
- Exchange rates are close to a random walk out of sample (Meese & Rogoff 1983; Rossi 2013, JEL).
- Technical-rule profits had disappeared for filter and moving-average rules by the early 1990s (Neely, Weller & Ulrich 2009, JFQA).
- Cross-sectional currency momentum earned up to 10% p.a. historically, but transaction costs partly explain it and limits to arbitrage are effective (Menkhoff et al. 2012, JFE).
- Carry earns a premium but carries crash risk (Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen 2008).
- Low dimensionality: dollar and carry factors dominate (Lustig, Roussanov & Verdelhan 2011; Verdelhan 2018).

Implication:
- A generic OHLC model with IC around 0.02 is very unlikely to clear costs, swap markup and 20.315% tax with only about 10 currencies.
- The cost advantage is real: about 1 bp per round trip on majors versus 10 bps or more in JP stocks. But it mainly helps a high-turnover signal, which Kronos has not shown elsewhere.
- The most plausible value-add is better volatility forecasts than HAR-RV/GARCH for volatility-targeted sizing. FX volatility is persistent and well measured from free tick data (Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003; Corsi 2009).
risks: Cross-account contagion: GMO Coin's FX 説明書 (§14) lets it stop withdrawals and dispose of the client's cash and crypto held at GMO Coin to cover unpaid FX debt. A weekend or flash gap through the loss-cut could hit any other capital held at GMO Coin. Mitigations: keep FX gross leverage ≤2–3x, or trade FX at a different broker.

Statistical power: with about 10 currencies, the pre-registered RankIC rule (Newey-West t ≥ 3) needs IC of about 0.05 at 1 day or about 0.16 at 12 days on the dev window. A 'no' result is the likely outcome for ranking and should be pre-declared as uninformative unless power is stated.

Cost model uncertainty: GMO Coin spreads are variable and unpublished, and the only figures found are third-party and possibly stale. The API fee is 0.4 bps per round trip. Spreads widen in off-hours. Slippage on market orders is unknown. The swap markup is probably the largest cost for multi-day holds.

Execution timing: daily bars close at 06:00 JST, near the rollover when spreads are widest (Saxo USD/JPY 60 sen from 04:00 to 07:59 JST). A 'signal at close, fill at next open' backtest would overstate fills. Execution must be delayed to 08:00/09:00 JST or later, and the lag modelled.

Gap and tail risk: weekend closures of about 49 hours, holiday flash events (e.g. 2019-01-03 JPY), the SNB-2015 type of risk if CHF is in the universe, price-feed halts with fills at the resumption price, and loss-cut not guaranteed (negative balance possible).

Data alignment: GMO 06:00 JST bars (fixed year-round), Dukascopy UTC, HistData EST without DST and the NY 17:00 convention all differ. Kronos uses weekday/day timestamp features, and its FX pretraining conventions are unknown. GMO bars before April 2023 are backfilled, of unknown provenance.
Universe drift: GMO added 7 pairs on 2026-05-18, mid-holdout. The universe must be fixed ex ante as the 14 pairs available since 2023, or survivorship and look-ahead creep in.
EM pairs: very high spreads and swaps (TRY), a 10,000-unit API minimum, and dealer trading restrictions in crises (GMO ERR-143 '規制中').

Terms drift: GMO changed its API fee basis and minimum order sizes after the 2023 launch. OANDA revamped status tiers in 2025 and closed MT4. Saxo's fixed spreads started 2026-05. These terms can change again. A tighter regulatory leverage cap was discussed in 2017; no 2026 change was found.

Operations: the strategy must run from the laptop at a fixed JST time each day, and missed runs leave positions unmanaged. Saxo needs an interactive OAuth login when refresh tokens lapse. MT4/MT5 routes need Windows.
Tax and accounting: FX gains fall in 先物取引に係る雑所得等 at 20.315%. FX losses cannot offset crypto gains (総合課税), and vice versa. FX is a separate return schedule.
Protocol: the Kronos paper's FX evaluation tables cover July 2024 onward, inside the sealed window. Anyone reading them before pre-registration contaminates the study.

claims.source: https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12587 (Verdelhan, The Share of Systematic Variation in Bilateral Exchange Rates, JF); see also https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhr068

claims.claim: MT4/MT5 FX brokers in Japan: FXTF (MT4), JFX (MT5; MT4 ended 2026-08-19), OANDA (MT5; MT4 new accounts closed), 楽天証券 (MT4), 外為ファイネスト (MT4/MT5), アヴァトレード・ジャパン (MT4/MT5). Minimum unit is 1,000.

checks.correction: OANDA: MT5 only. MT4 new orders were halted on 2026-09-25 and MT4 ends 2026-11-27. Add FOREX.com Japan (MT5 only since its MT4 ended 2026-10-16). The JFX date is unconfirmed by a primary source.

- FXTF: MT4. Its MT5 currently covers only commodity and crypto CFDs, with FX 'planned'.
- JFX: MT5; MT4 ended 2026-08-19.
- OANDA: MT5 on the Tokyo server. It is ending MT4 entirely, with trading ending 2026-11-27, not just closing it to new accounts.
- 楽天: MT4.
- 外為ファイネスト: MT4 and MT5.
- AvaTrade: MT4 and MT5.
- Minimum unit 1,000 (OANDA MXN/JPY and CNH/JPY: 10,000).

new_findings.finding: Kronos's FX pretraining data overlaps every pre-seal GMO bar. Table 13 of the Kronos paper lists a 'Foreign Exchange' pretraining set of 1,023 assets and 462.4M bars (5-min to weekly), starting 2020-01-31 and running to June 2024. GMO Coin's bars from 2023-01-02 to 2024-06-30, and any 2020-02 to 2024-06 window from Dukascopy or HistData, are therefore probably inside Kronos's training data.
new_findings.impact: A dev or validation window between 2020-02 and 2024-06 is in-sample for the pretrained model and would inflate IC. The only clean out-of-sample FX data is pre-2020 third-party data or the sealed post-June-2024 window. The pre-registration must put the dev window before 2020 (Dukascopy/HistData) or declare 2020-02 to 2024-06 contaminated. This also undercuts using GMO's own 2023–24 bars for development.
new_findings.source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.02739v1 (Table 13; Appendix D 'pre-training data … extends up to June 2024')

new_findings.finding: An unpaid FX shortfall can halt the whole GMO Coin service, not just consume its collateral. サービス基本約款 (ver 2026-10-30) Art. 17 allows set-off of any claim at any time without notice. Art. 22(2)(19) allows GMO to suspend, restrict or terminate all or part of 本サービス if a 不足金 is not paid by its due date. Art. 22(5) allows disposal of client assets, including liquidating crypto. 外国為替FX取引約款 Art. 18 requires losses beyond margin to be paid immediately.
new_findings.impact: FX gap risk at GMO is directly coupled to everything else held in the same account: an FX debt could freeze it. Ring-fencing needs a different broker (e.g. Saxo OpenAPI) or a hard low-leverage cap. This strengthens summary point (6) and is a reason to weigh Saxo despite its weaker support.

new_findings.finding: Swap asymmetry in bps is far larger for the exotic legs of the 10-currency JPY universe. Official GMO swaps for 2026-11-05 (per 10k units, 1 day): TRY/JPY +24.1/−37.1, ZAR/JPY +11/−20, MXN/JPY +14.1/−16.1, against USD/JPY +106/−142. At assumed TRY/JPY 3.5 and ZAR/JPY 8.5, the buy–sell gap is about 3.7 and 1.1 bps/day of notional. Against the mid-swap that is about 31 and 9 bps per position over a 12-trading-day hold, compared with about 2 bps for majors.
new_findings.impact: TRY (and arguably ZAR) legs are cost-prohibitive for a 12-day long-short book, before counting their wide spreads. Excluding them shrinks the cross-section to about 8 names and lowers statistical power further.

new_findings.finding: GMO's daily bar boundary and swap cut-off (06:00 JST) fall inside the official illiquid window. Saxo Japan widens USD/JPY from 0.2 sen to 60 sen (EUR/JPY and AUD/JPY to 100 sen) from 04:00 to 07:59 JST Mon–Sat. GMO 1-day klines open at 06:00 JST, swaps accrue after 06:00, and GMO trading reopens Monday 07:00. GMO 1-hour bars exist only from 2023-10-28, about 8 months before the seal.
new_findings.impact: A backtest that trades at daily closes would understate costs. Execution must be scheduled in liquid hours (after about 08:00 JST), and the cost and fill model can only be calibrated intraday on about 8 months of pre-seal GMO hourly data.
new_findings.source: https://api.coin.z.com/fxdocs/ (KLine: 日本時間朝6：00に新しい日付に切替; 1min–1hour from 20231028) ; https://www.home.saxo/ja-jp/rates-and-conditions/forex/spreads-and-commissions ; https://coin.z.com/jp/corp/product/info/fx/swap/

new_findings.finding: GMO spreads can be measured first-hand at no cost. The unauthenticated public /v1/ticker returns live bid and ask for all 21 pairs, and the klines return separate BID and ASK OHLC back to 2023-01-02. The third-party spread table in FX-8 is labelled 原則固定 and appears to be legacy FX Prime data, while GMO Coin officially quotes 変動制.
new_findings.impact: The low-confidence FX-8 spread inputs can be replaced with measured GMO spreads: live from the ticker, and historically from pre-seal BID/ASK bars. That makes the cost model first-party and auditable at zero cost.

new_findings.finding: GMO can discontinue FX pairs. サービス基本約款 Art. 21(3) applies the delisting procedure (at least 30 days' notice) to FX currency pairs (取扱通貨ペアを廃止する場合について準用).
new_findings.impact: 'FX has no delistings' is not strictly true at broker level. The pre-registered universe needs a rule for a dropped pair. Low probability, low impact.

new_findings.finding: GMO's loss-cut fee is ¥0.05 per unit regardless of price. As a share of notional that is about 1.4% for TRY/JPY at an assumed 3.5, about 0.6% for ZAR or MXN, about 12% for HUF/JPY at an assumed 0.4, and about 0.03% for USD/JPY at 150. New orders also need 5% margin (注文必要証拠金), versus 4% to maintain a position.
new_findings.impact: Negligible at about 2x gross leverage, but punitive for exotics if a loss-cut ever triggers. It supports keeping leverage low and excluding HUF and TRY.

new_findings.finding: The 30-day API-fee waiver starts when the FX API key is created, even if no orders are placed ('注文または注文変更を行わない場合でも、無料トライアルが開始します').
new_findings.impact: Create the key only when live trading begins, or the free month is lost. Minor.

new_findings.finding: Tax may change. The bill moving crypto under the FIEA (金商法・資金決済法改正) passed on 2026-07-15. Under the 令和8年度税制改正大綱, 特定暗号資産 gains move to 20.315% separate taxation from 1 January of the year after the amended FIEA takes effect; commentators expect 2028. Whether crypto derivatives will join FX in 先物取引に係る雑所得等 (allowing FX and crypto-derivative gains and losses to offset) is not stated in the sources checked. The separate FX rate stays 20.315% after the 2027 surtax restructure.
new_findings.impact: FX-31's 'cannot offset crypto' holds through at least 2027 but may change from about 2028. Re-check when cabinet orders are issued. It does not change Phase-0 feasibility.

new_findings.finding: Crypto tax reform is enacted. 令和8年法律第12号 passed 2026-03-31. The FIEA/PSA amendment passed 2026-07-15 and was promulgated 2026-07-23; its crypto provisions take effect on a Cabinet Order date within 1 year. From 1 January of the following year (expected 2028-01-01), derivatives on 特定暗号資産 move into 先物取引に係る雑所得等, the same category as OTC FX. Spot 特定暗号資産 move to a separate 20% category with their own 3-year carryforward.
new_findings.impact: FX-31's 'cannot offset crypto' goes stale from about 2028. Gains from 暗号資産FX or レバレッジ trading would then net against FX losses, and both would be taxed at 20.315%. That changes the after-tax value of FX experiments. Spot-crypto gains still cannot be netted with FX.

new_findings.finding: GMO Coin's quoted spreads can be measured from its own public 1-min BID/ASK klines, and they have widened since 2024. Liquid-hours (09:00–23:59 JST) median for USD/JPY was 0.2 sen on 2024-03-13 and 2024-06-12, and 0.5 sen on 2026-11-04/05. Nov 2026 values: EUR/JPY 0.5, GBP/JPY 0.9, AUD/JPY 0.7, NZD/JPY 0.9, CAD/JPY 0.8, CHF/JPY 1.1, TRY/JPY 0.9, ZAR/JPY 1.0, MXN/JPY 0.3 sen; EUR/USD 0.5 and GBP/USD 0.9 pips. Adding the 0.4 bp API fee, at assumed price levels a round trip costs about 0.7–1.4 bps for majors and crosses, about 4 bps for MXN, about 12 bps for ZAR and about 25–30 bps for TRY. The summary's TRY figure (about 120 bps) came from legacy FX Prime data.
new_findings.impact: Replaces the unusable minkabu figures with GMO's own data. The majors cost range holds, but GMO is now about 2.5x its 2024 USD/JPY spread. Spreads during the sealed window were not looked at. Pre-window spreads from 2023-10-28 to 2024-06-30 can be measured without touching sealed data.
new_findings.source: https://forex-api.coin.z.com/public/v1/klines?symbol=USD_JPY&priceType=ASK&interval=1min&date=20261104 (and BID; same for other symbols and dates 20240313, 20240612, 20261105)

new_findings.finding: GMO spreads blow out exactly at its daily-bar boundary. USD/JPY was about 16.3 sen during 06:00–07:59 JST and 3.0 sen during 08:00–08:59 on 2026-11-04/05, against 0.5 sen otherwise. The 2024 samples show 13–21 sen in the same window. Other pairs widen similarly, e.g. GBP/JPY to about 18 sen and EUR/USD to about 7 pips.
new_findings.impact: A daily strategy that fills at GMO's 06:00 JST bar open would pay 30x or more the normal spread. Execution has to be scheduled at or after about 09:00 JST, and backtests must not assume fills at the daily open.

new_findings.finding: GMO publishes official day-by-day buy and sell swap history through the endpoint behind its swap calendar, from at least 2023. Half the buy/sell gap is about 0.12–0.23 bps/day per side on JPY crosses in 2023–24 and about 0.10–0.15 on 2026-11-06, at assumed price levels.
new_findings.impact: Gives an official, reproducible holding-cost series for backtests instead of a third-party snapshot. The current carry markup is slightly below the researcher's estimate.

new_findings.finding: Saxo's parent has changed hands and Saxo is retreating in APAC. J. Safra Sarasin closed a ~71% stake in Saxo Bank A/S on 2026-03-02 and agreed in July 2026 to buy the remaining ~28.69%. The Saxo JP site now says Saxo A/S 'は、J. Safra Sarasin Groupの一員です'. Saxo's June 2024 strategic review covered Australia, Japan and Hong Kong. It was followed by closing the Hong Kong office (Sept 2024) and selling 80.1% of Saxo Australia to DMA (2025, rebranded Totality). Japan still operates as a 100% subsidiary. Its account opening was suspended in October 2026 because of an identity-verification outage and resumed 2026-10-24.
new_findings.impact: There is continuity risk for the Saxo backup route. No Japan exit has been announced, but Saxo Japan was in scope of the review that ended the other two APAC units.

new_findings.finding: Saxo's route has costs and operational burdens the summary misses. OpenAPI orders are rejected unless pre-trade disclaimers are handled, enforced since May 2025. 1-minute chart history is cut to 6 months (LIVE expected 2026-11-03). SIM has no market data. Saxo also charges 資金調達金利 on unrealized P&L carried overnight: paid on losses, received on gains, with payments larger than receipts. Its own swaps are also asymmetric. Only 5 pairs have fixed spreads.
new_findings.impact: Saxo is not a usable historical-data source. Order logic must handle disclaimers. Holding costs are higher than spread-only estimates suggest, which further favours GMO as the primary route.

new_findings.finding: MT4 is being retired at Japanese brokers in 2026. OANDA stopped MT4 new orders on 2026-09-25 and ends MT4 on 2026-11-27. It made MT5 OTP mandatory on 2026-10-31 and has revalued MT5 margin daily since 2026-06-08. FOREX.com Japan (StoneX証券) ended MT4 on 2026-10-16. MetaQuotes officially documents running the MT5 terminal on Linux via Wine (mt5linux.sh), but the MetaTrader5 Python package remains Windows-only.
new_findings.impact: Any MetaTrader route now means MT5, with a Windows or Wine dependency. This strengthens the case for GMO's native REST/WebSocket API. Wine on the x86-64 laptop is an unofficial fallback, not an option on the ARM server.

new_findings.finding: 松井証券 has an FX API (since 2022-12) for orders, order and position queries, and rates, using access-token auth. Access is only through third-party vendors or advisory services under a separate API利用許諾契約, reviewed case by case, with vendor-specific fees. It is not self-service for retail. It is likely one of FFAJ's 7 API providers.
new_findings.impact: This is an extra but impractical route. It does not change the GMO-first conclusion, but the survey of API brokers should mention it.

new_findings.finding: GMO Coin is reorganising its corporate structure. It is preparing a TSE listing. GMO Financial HD transferred its system development and operations business to GMO Coin by absorption-type split effective 2026-04-01. Its president stepped down from the GMO-FH role on 2026-03-19. No change to the FX product or API terms was found. The FX docs' last change is still 2026-05-16, and press releases since then concern crypto only, e.g. 代用暗号資産 for crypto derivatives from 2026-07-25.
new_findings.impact: Low. Re-check FX terms after any listing-related changes. The new crypto-collateral feature applies to crypto derivatives, not 外国為替FX, so FX-12's cross-account debt link is unchanged.

new_findings.finding:
GMO's FX terms (約款, rev. 2025-02-08) give GMO broad discretion:
- It may stop or refuse new orders at any time in light of its own risk, including cover-provider outages (第8条4).
- It may refuse orders it deems inappropriate (第11条3).
- It may cancel fills at off-market prices (第13条).
- It may change trading rules at any time (第19条2).
- It may change or revoke the API licence by notice, without liability (第20条).
API use is personal only; commercial use is banned (第21条3). The docs have a dedicated 'API取引規制' error (ERR-5125) and allow throttling of 'heavy' users. API support is by inquiry form only, not chat.
new_findings.impact: All execution risk sits with one dealer, and the cross-default clause (§14) links FX to any other assets held there. A restriction or outage at GMO hits everything held there at once. This is not a deal-breaker for a small daily book, but it calls for a manual fallback and for not keeping all capital at GMO.

new_findings.finding:
GMO's API terms changed during the sealed window.
- At the 2023-10-28 launch: fee ¥0.002 per unit; minimum 10,000 units (100,000 for TRY, ZAR, MXN).
- A user blog dated 2024-09-12 still hit the 10,000-unit minimum.
- Now: 0.002% of notional and a 100-unit minimum.
No announcement date for either change was found.
new_findings.impact: Historical backtests over 2024-07 to 2026-10 cannot assume today's terms for the whole window. At 2023 price levels, a 10-cross book at the old minimums was about ¥11–12M gross notional, needing about ¥0.55–0.6M of order margin at 5%. That is infeasible at ¥500k and about 11x leverage at ¥1M. The old per-unit fee was about 0.13 bps per side on USD/JPY but about 2.4–4 bps per side on ZAR, MXN and TRY. The study should state that it uses current terms, or model the change.

new_findings.finding: GMO's free 30-day API trial starts the moment the first FX API key is created, even if no order is ever placed. It is for first-time users only and can be changed or ended without notice.
new_findings.impact: Do not create the FX API key during development; create it when forward or live trading starts, or the free month is lost.

new_findings.finding: GMO publishes its own daily swap history. The site JSON behind the swap calendar's 'past swaps' view has buy and sell values per productId and date. The data exists for at least 2023-11, for example 2023-11-24 with USD/JPY +209/−262 per 10k units. The productId-to-symbol mapping and the unit basis for the exotics are undocumented. For example, the 2023 TRY/ZAR/MXN values look like per-10k quotes, while the page now says per-100k.
new_findings.impact: This is a primary source for swap-cost modelling, replacing the 2023 minkabu snapshot (which has a 10x USD/JPY error). Mapping and units must be validated before use, and the sealed-window protocol still applies to the 2024-07 to 2026-10 dates.

new_findings.finding: GMO's own data can measure its spreads directly. Klines come as separate BID and ASK OHLC, with 1-minute bars from 2023-10-28, and the unauthenticated /public/v1/ticker returns live bid and ask.
new_findings.impact: This removes reliance on the low-confidence third-party spread figures in FX-8. It gives spreads by time of day for the pre-window period (2023-10-28 to 2024-06-30) and live from now. Bar-close BID/ASK pairs are only an approximation of the quoted spread.

new_findings.finding:
Execution-timing trap.
- GMO's daily bars and swap roll at 06:00 JST all year. That is inside the NY-close and early-Tokyo window where Japanese retail spreads widen: Saxo quotes USD/JPY at 60 sen against 0.2 sen during 04:00–07:59 JST, and GMOクリック at 3.8 against 0.2 sen outside 09:00–27:00.
- GMO's hours (Mon 07:00 to Sat 05:59) do not shift with DST. In US winter its 06:00 bar boundary is one hour before the NY close at 07:00 JST.
new_findings.impact: A daily signal must be executed hours after the bar closes, for example in the Tokyo morning or evening when the user's laptop is actually on. The backtest must model that lag and a spread that depends on time of day. Bar boundaries also differ from Dukascopy and HistData conventions (HistData uses EST without DST).

new_findings.finding: Saxo Japan onboarding is disrupted. An identity-verification outage blocked account opening until about 2026-10-24 09:00. A notice dated 2026-11-06 says account opening is still 'taking longer than usual'.
new_findings.impact: The fallback route has an uncertain onboarding time right now. Do not plan a Saxo SIM-to-LIVE path without extra weeks of slack.

new_findings.finding:
Saxo LIVE OpenAPI uses the OAuth authorization-code flow.
- Documented sample: access token expires_in 1200 s; refresh_token_expires_in 2400 s.
- Each refresh issues a new token pair. Once the refresh token lapses, the full browser login must be repeated.
- 24-hour developer-portal tokens work only on SIM.
- Saxo JP gives no OpenAPI support, and its usage conditions say 'contact us'.
new_findings.impact: Unattended Saxo trading needs an always-on process that refreshes in under about 40 minutes. A laptop sleeps, so Saxo becomes a daily manual-login workflow. GMO's HMAC keys do not expire.

new_findings.finding:
October 2026 breach of a common MT4/MT5 host. GMO Internet's 'お名前.com デスクトップクラウド' is a Windows VPS widely used to run MT4/MT5 around the clock.
- 2026-10-20: a malicious program was found.
- From 2026-10-21: all plans suspended.
- 26,739 servers possibly affected.
- Customers reported unauthorized operations on trading accounts using MT4/MT5 credentials stored on the servers.
- Restart date undetermined (second notice 2026-10-22; Nikkei 2026-10-24).
new_findings.impact: The usual workaround for Windows-only MT4/MT5, a rented Windows VPS, has a recent, demonstrated credential-theft risk. This strengthens the case for running GMO's REST API locally, with IP restriction and order-only key permissions (both supported).

new_findings.finding: Crypto tax reform (令和8年度). Gains on 'specified crypto assets' (spot, investment trusts and derivatives at registered firms) are to move to 20% separate taxation with a 3-year loss carry-forward. It applies from 1 January of the year after the amended FIEA takes effect, which DIR expects in 2028. DIR (2026-02-06) says spot-crypto losses cannot be netted with other financial products. No source found says whether crypto-derivative P&L will join 先物取引に係る雑所得等 and so net against FX.
new_findings.impact: FX-31's 'FX losses cannot offset crypto gains' holds through at least 2027 but may change from about 2028. Re-check before any multi-year after-tax comparison.

new_findings.finding: JPY can move between GMO's crypto and FX accounts through the crypto API (POST /private/v1/account/transfer, at most once per 3 minutes, direction set by transferType). The FX API has no transfer endpoint.
new_findings.impact: Margin top-ups and sweeps can be automated, but only with a crypto-API key that has transfer rights. That would give the FX process a key with transfer rights over the whole account. Keeping transfers manual is safer, and at low leverage they are rarely needed.

new_findings.finding: Hedging and position-count trap. GMO FX allows 両建. Plain new orders open new positions, so reducing exposure needs closeOrder with settlePosition IDs, or speedOrder with isHedgeable=false (the default). Caps: 1,000 open positions and 2,000 live orders; unfilled orders expire after 30 days.
new_findings.impact: A naive rebalancer that sends opposite-side new orders would end up hedged. It would pay the swap markup on both legs, pay API fees twice, and post margin on the larger leg. Easy to avoid, but it must be coded.

new_findings.finding: Eligibility. The GMO FX account is an add-on application with My Number. My Number is not needed again if it was already submitted for crypto derivatives. Screening is against unpublished '当社所定の口座開設基準' and is done on business days. No minimum balance applies (minimum transfer ¥1). JPY instant deposits and withdrawals are free, with ¥400 for large withdrawals.
new_findings.impact: No deal-breaker was found, but approval is not guaranteed and the criteria are unknown.

new_findings.finding: Public reports of GMO FX API reliability are scarce. One 2024-09 blog reported API keys it had created disappearing (cause unknown) and called variable spreads plus minimum order sizes the main drawbacks. No outage reports were found, but the search was cut short when the session's web-search budget ran out.
new_findings.impact: Reliability is unknown rather than shown to be good. Plan a forward period to measure rejections (ERR-5125, ERR-5218), maintenance responses (ERR-5201, ERR-5202) and fill quality before scaling up.

title: US stocks and ETFs through a licensed Japanese broker with an API

research.market: US-listed stocks and ETFs (NYSE, Nasdaq, NYSE Arca/American) traded by a Japan-resident individual through FSA-registered Japanese brokers with a trading API
research.summary: Feasible at JPY 500k, but only at one cost level. Four FSA-registered brokers offer US-stock APIs to Japan residents. (1) ウィブル証券 (Webull JP): cloud REST/MQTT/gRPC API that runs on Linux with no gateway. US commission has been zero since 2026-07-27, stated as permanent. FX is 15 sen/USD each way. It has 特定口座, fractional shares on about 3,000 names, and margin/short through the API (added 2026-04-25). There is no private API paper account. (2) IBKR証券 (IBSJ): TWS API via IB Gateway, or the Web API via a local Java gateway; both run on Linux. Tiered is USD 0.0035/share with a USD 0.35 minimum; Fixed is USD 0.005/share with a USD 1.00 minimum. It has the best paper account and MOC/MOO orders. There is no 特定口座, and US margin/short is still 'full availability coming soon'. (3) moomoo証券: the OpenD gateway runs on Ubuntu/CentOS. Commission is 0.132%/side, with paper trading and 特定口座. US shorts are allowed on 1,000+ margin names. (4) サクソバンク証券: 0.088% commission with a USD 1.10 minimum, 0.25% FX, shorts via CFDs only, and no API support. Planning assumptions: a 10-name S&P 500 book and an unchecked JPY 150/USD. At JPY 500k the all-in round trip is about 4-9 bps at Webull, 25-30 bps at IBSJ Tiered, 29-34 bps at moomoo, and 63-74 bps at IBSJ Fixed or Saxo. At JPY 3M, IBSJ Tiered falls to about 7-12 bps. Survivorship-free daily data with delisted names and historical S&P 500 membership fits the budget: Sharadar Prices, 10-year tier, USD 19/mo or USD 199/yr (about JPY 2,500-2,850/mo). Full history from 1997 costs USD 299/yr (about JPY 3,740/mo). Kronos pretraining covered 8,725 Nasdaq and 7,073 NYSE instruments from 2000 to June 2024, about 38% of all records. Any US evaluation before July 2024 is therefore in-sample, and clean data exists only in the sealed window and in forward tests. The realistic use is daily or weekly cross-sectional ranking of S&P 500 / Russell 1000 names. The edge prior is weak: this is the most competitive equity market. An IC of about 0.02 gives roughly 5-7 bps/day gross for a top-decile book (my estimate), which could survive only at Webull or IBSJ-at-JPY-3M cost levels. Operational frictions: the US session runs 23:30-06:00 JST (22:30-05:00 during US DST). Passkey login has been mandatory at Japanese brokers since July 2026, and unattended gateway re-login is unverified. IBSJ requires self-filed 一般口座 tax on a moving-average cost basis. Blinding note: one item to disclose is under risks.

brokers.broker: ウィブル証券 Webull Securities Japan (関東財務局長(金商)第48号)
brokers.api: Webull OpenAPI (JP): Trading API + Market Data API; official Python (3.8-3.14) and Java SDKs; MCP server/agent skills also offered
brokers.api_kind: Cloud REST over HTTPS (HMAC-SHA256 signed with App Key/Secret; optional 2FA token verified in the Webull app), MQTT streaming quotes, gRPC order-event push; no local gateway
brokers.linux: Yes - OS-agnostic cloud API (api.webull.co.jp); Python SDK
brokers.eligibility: Japan-resident individual with a Webull JP account. The OpenAPI application is reviewed in 1-2 business days. Key generation needs an SMS code and the trading password. The old docs say keys are valid 45 days by default, and a token becomes INVALID after 15 days with no API calls. US margin needs its own application (1-3 business days) and a minimum 委託保証金 of JPY 300,000 equivalent in USD. Both 特定口座 and 一般口座 are offered; the API field account_tax_type takes GENERAL or SPECIFIC.
brokers.paper_env: Only a UAT test environment with publicly shared test accounts, whose orders and positions may change at any time. No private API paper account is documented. A forward test would need small live orders, which is cheap here because commission is zero, or an internal simulated ledger fed by live quotes.
brokers.fees: Commission: 0 on US stocks/ETFs, cash and margin, since 2026-07-27. Pass-through fees: SEC USD 0.0000206 x sale proceeds; FINRA TAF USD 0.000195/share sold (min 0.01, max 9.79); CAT USD 0.000003/share. FX: 15 sen/USD each way, about 10 bps; paid once if pre-converted to USD, or on every trade if settled in JPY. Margin: buy interest 4.5%/yr, borrow fee from 1.5%/yr, day-trade margin 0%. No API surcharge. Nasdaq Basic market data via the API is free.

capital.min_unit: 1 share for whole-share orders (no board lot). (a) Commission should stay at or below about 5 bps per side. (b) Whole-share rounding should stay within about 10% of target weight, otherwise fractional shares are needed. An optional long-short version adds 10 shorts and needs a margin account above the JPY 300k / USD 2.5k floors.
capital.capital_needed_jpy: Webull (zero commission + fractional): about JPY 300k-500k. IBSJ Tiered: about JPY 1M, since orders of about USD 700 or more bring the USD 0.35 minimum to about 5 bps/side. IBSJ Fixed or Saxo: about JPY 3M (orders of USD 2,000-2,200 or more). moomoo never gets below 13.2 bps/side, so it suits only low turnover. All at an assumed JPY 150/USD.
capital.at_500k: About USD 333 per name for 10 names. Round-trip all-in for an S&P 500 name: Webull about 4-9 bps (feasible, fractional available). IBSJ Tiered about 25-30 bps and moomoo about 29-34 bps (weekly turnover at most). IBSJ Fixed about 63-68 bps and Saxo about 69-74 bps (not feasible). Without fractional shares, names priced above about USD 333 cannot be held at equal weight. Long-short is possible above the margin floors but has thin buffer at 30% maintenance.
capital.at_1m: About USD 667 per name. Webull about 4-9 bps; IBSJ Tiered about 15-20; moomoo about 29-34; IBSJ Fixed about 33-38; Saxo about 36-41. Feasible at Webull and IBSJ Tiered, marginal elsewhere.
capital.at_3m: About USD 2,000 per name. Webull about 4-9 bps; IBSJ Tiered about 7-12; IBSJ Fixed about 13-18; Saxo about 21-26; moomoo about 29-34. Feasible at Webull or IBSJ; IBSJ adds paper trading and MOC/MOO. 20-name books and long-short become practical.

costs.round_trip_bps: Typical S&P 500 name, 10-name book, at JPY 500k / 1M / 3M: Webull 4-9 / 4-9 / 4-9; IBSJ Tiered 25-30 / 15-20 / 7-12; IBSJ Fixed 63-68 / 33-38 / 13-18; moomoo 29-34 at every size; Saxo Classic 69-74 / 36-41 / 21-26. Excludes the one-off FX conversion and taxes. Small caps and ETFs differ: spreads are much wider for small caps and near 1 bp for the largest ETFs.
costs.breakdown: Commissions per side: IBSJ Tiered USD 0.35 minimum plus about USD 0.003/share exchange and clearing fees; IBSJ Fixed USD 1.00 minimum; moomoo 13.2 bps; Saxo max(0.088%, USD 1.10); Webull 0. Sale-side regulatory fees: SEC 0.206 bps of proceeds plus FINRA TAF USD 0.000195/share (min USD 0.01), together about 0.3-0.5 bps per round trip on small tickets. Spread and slippage, assumed 3-8 bps per round trip: the dollar-volume-weighted effective spread for S&P 500 stocks was 2.73-3.22 bps (quoted 3.55 bps) in a Dec-2015 study, and I add 0-5 bps of open/close execution noise. IBKR MOC/MOO orders avoid the spread against the auction print. FX, one-off if USD is kept: Webull 15 sen/USD (about 10 bps each way), moomoo about 3 sen (about 2 bps), IBSJ auto-conversion about 3 bps, Saxo 25 bps. If trades are settled in JPY, these are paid on every trade, so use USD settlement. Market impact is negligible at USD 300-2,000 tickets.
costs.holding_costs: Cash long-only: no custody or maintenance fees at any of the four brokers. ADR depositary fees run USD 0.01-0.05/share. The main holding risk is USD/JPY exposure. IBSJ pays 0% on USD cash of USD 10k or less. Margin long: IBSJ 5.38%/yr (USD 100k or less, 2026-11-08); moomoo 4.5%/yr (stated as of 2024-10-28); Webull 4.5%/yr; day-trade margin 0% at moomoo/Webull. Short: borrow fee from 1.5%/yr at moomoo/Webull, varying daily by name; IBSJ charges a per-name market rate with no rebate on the first USD 100k of proceeds. Short holders pay dividends. Saxo CFDs charge benchmark-based financing (exact markup unverified). No swap or roll costs for cash equities. Taxes: 20.315% on gains; US dividends 10% withheld plus Japanese tax.

research.shorting: Available, but only on margin and with conditions. IBSJ: eligible US stocks under Japanese rules, initial 50% / maintenance 30%, NLV of at least JPY 300k, per-name borrow fee, no proceeds rebate under USD 100k, liquidation without margin calls, and a site banner saying margin is still 'full availability coming soon'. IBSJ share CFDs (DMA) are an alternative. moomoo: US 信用 shorting on 1,000+ names, minimum 委託保証金 USD 2,500, borrow fee from 1.5%/yr, 30% maintenance; the API exposes SELL_SHORT/BUY_BACK and JP short sub-accounts; micro shares cannot be shorted. Webull: US margin shorting with a minimum JPY 300k-equivalent USD; borrow fee from 1.5%/yr; ONE_DAY margin (0% interest, auto-closed before the close) or INDEFINITE; API side SHORT available since 2026-04-25 (individual-user scope to verify). Saxo: no cash-stock shorting; shorts via single-stock CFDs (20% margin, max 5x, financing, separate tax pool). US-side rules: Reg SHO locate requirement; the Rule 201 price test (a 10% fall from the prior close bars shorts at or below the national best bid for the rest of that day and the next); forced buy-ins and recalls; hard-to-borrow fees can spike. A JPY 500k long-short book is technically possible but has little cushion; JPY 1-3M is more realistic.
